newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Investors keen on Merrill Lynch kangaroo bond.
newsitem.headline: Investors keen on Merrill Lynch kangaroo bond.

text.p: Merrill Lynch and Co Inc said that its March 2002 fungible kangaroo bond met strong investor demand and saw the issue increased to A$150 million from an original A$100 million.
The bonds, which were priced on Thursday, are fungible with and original A$200 million transaction issued in April, bringing the total issue size to A$350 million.
"The deal was increased in repsonse to very solid and widely spread investor interest," said Tim Martin, Director Global Debt Markets at Merrill Lynch in Sydney.

The latest issue was priced earlier on Thursday at 36 basis points over the March 2002 Australian government bond to yield 6.425 percent and compared with a 40 basis point spread when the first offering was made in April.
The bonds, which carry a coupon of 7.625 percent, are rated AA minus and Aa3.
Martin said the bonds had all been placed and the feedback from the market has been very positive.
Earlier this week Merrill Lynch reported second quarter net earnings of US$481 million, the highest of any quarter in the firm's history. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
